result.title: Strong Fused Performance Can Mask Branch Collapse in a Dual-View Heart-Sound Classifier: A Three-Part Diagnostic Protocol
result.summary: Fusion models are usually judged by their fused score, a practice that assumes that every branch has learned something useful. We show that this assumption can fail silently in dual-view heart-sound classification. In AudioFuse, which fuses a spectrogram transformer with a waveform CNN, the spectrogram branch is unused despite strong fused performance when both branches are trained from scratch. We introduce a three-part diagnostic for branch collapse: whether deleting a branch changes the fused score, whether a linear probe on its features beats an untrained copy of the same branch, and whether the branch can learn its view when trained alone. Deleting the branch has negligible effect, and probing its features shows little improvement over an identically initialised, untrained copy. Yet the same architecture trained alone exceeds 0.9 AUC, so its view is learnable, while the jointly trained model is near chance when it must rely on this branch. Update statistics and an initialisation experiment point to an early optimisation imbalance. Moving a strong artificial label cue from one input to the other can switch which branch the model relies on, even though the branch architectures stay the same. We observe branch collapse on PhysioNet, but the full diagnostic is not met on ICBHI or CirCor. Fused performance alone therefore cannot establish that every branch learned a meaningful representation, and we recommend reporting branch deletion and an untrained-control probe alongside it.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在双视角心音分类模型 AudioFuse 中发现：即使融合分数很好，谱图分支实际上未被使用；作者据此提出三段式诊断（删除分支是否改变融合分数、分支特征线性探针是否优于同初始化的未训练对照、单独训练能否学会本视角），并归因于早期优化失衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 「融合分数好但某分支塌缩」与 LVR 关注的视觉旁路、信息坍缩、贡献分配高度同构，其删除实验与未训练对照探针可供核查 VLM 中视觉分支是否真的被使用，但需注意原文为心音音频任务、无 VLM 与 latent 生成。
